intent.raw_query: Iceland Northern Lights and hot springs, $3500 couple, January 2026

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover in real time to maximize your viewing experience. Hot chocolate and warm blankets provided.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Booking in advance is essential. The surreal lava field backdrop makes this one of Iceland's most iconic hot spring experiences.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. A truly authentic and affordable Icelandic bathing tradition.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Settlement Exhibition museum to dive into Norse culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The contrast of steaming hot springs against snow-dusted neon-hued peaks is utterly surreal and unforgettable.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Iceland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.afternoon: No afternoon activities — flight arrives late at night
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavik International Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and collect luggage. Take the budget-friendly Flybus shuttle (approx. 3,000 ISK) to Reykjavik and transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: N/A — in transit
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at the airport Keflavik terminal (sandwiches or soup from a kiosk to keep costs low, approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is arrival only. No sightseeing planned. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance since arrival is after 22:00. Pack light snacks for the journey to save money.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a slow start, walk along the nearby beachfront area around the resort to get oriented. Enjoy the dramatic winter coastline and black sand scenery — completely free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the famous Reykjanes Peninsula hot springs area. Head to the Blue Lagoon vicinity (exterior walk is free) or opt for the more budget-friendly Reykjadalur hot spring river trail if accessible. Alternatively, visit the free geothermal area at Gunnuhver mud pools on the Reykjanes Peninsula — steaming vents and boiling mud pools at no cost.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Keep an eye out for the Northern Lights after sunset (darkness falls early in January, around 16:00). Step outside around 21:00–23:00 on clear nights. Check the Icelandic Met Office aurora forecast app (free) for real-time alerts.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at the resort or nearby supermarket (Bonus or Kronan) — yogurt, skyr, bread, and fruit. Approx. 800–1,200 ISK.
meals.lunch: Pack a sandwich from the supermarket for the afternoon outing. Approx. 700–1,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook a simple meal at the resort if kitchen facilities are available, or try Pylsuvagninn (Icelandic hot dog stand) for an iconic and cheap dinner — approx. 500–800 ISK per hot dog.

day_by_day.notes: January days are very short in Iceland (roughly 5–6 hours of daylight). Plan outdoor sightseeing between 10:00–15:30 to maximize light. Layer up with thermal base layers, waterproof outer layers, and warm boots.

day_by_day.morning: Head into Reykjavik city center. Walk the iconic Laugavegur shopping street and visit Hallgrimskirkja Church — the exterior is free, and the tower viewing platform costs only 1,000 ISK. Stroll around the colorful old harbor area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sun Voyager sculpture (free) along the waterfront. Explore the Tjornin lake area and feed the ducks. Walk through the old town neighborhoods admiring the colorful corrugated iron houses. Visit Harpa Concert Hall exterior and free lobby area for stunning architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights hunt from a dark spot near the coastline or a short drive out of the city. Use the Vedur aurora app to track activity. If lights are not visible, enjoy a cozy evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Supermarket skyr with granola and coffee at the resort. Approx. 600–900 ISK.
meals.lunch: Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur — the famous Reykjavik hot dog stand near the harbor. Budget meal under 1,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Hlemmur Mathöll food hall — a budget-friendly option with various vendors offering smaller portions. Approx. 2,000–3,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Most of Reykjavik's best sights are free or very cheap. Avoid tourist trap restaurants near the main square — venture a block or two away for better prices.

day_by_day.morning: Golden Circle Day Trip (self-guided by renting a budget car or joining a shared tour). First stop: Thingvellir National Park — free entry, walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates, see Oxara River and historic parliament site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle to Geysir geothermal area — free to walk around and watch Strokkur geyser erupt every 5–10 minutes. Then drive to Gullfoss waterfall — free entry, one of Iceland's most spectacular waterfalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return toward Reykjavik. Stop at a quiet rural area on the way back for a Northern Lights viewing opportunity away from city light pollution. Arrive back at resort by 21:00.

meals.breakfast: Early supermarket breakfast before departure. Bread, cheese, and coffee. Approx. 700 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket eaten at Geysir or Gullfoss parking area. Approx. 800–1,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Simple self-catered dinner at resort. Pasta with canned tomato sauce and vegetables. Approx. 1,000–1,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Renting a small car for the day costs approx. 8,000–12,000 ISK split among travelers. Alternatively, shared Golden Circle bus tours start at around 8,000–10,000 ISK per person. Roads in January can be icy — drive cautiously and check road.is before departing.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula geothermal fields. Explore the Bridge Between Continents — a small footbridge spanning the fissure between tectonic plates (free). Walk around the surrounding lava fields.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Reykjanesviti Lighthouse, Iceland's oldest lighthouse, and the nearby dramatic coastal cliffs. Explore the Valahnukamol rock stacks and crashing Atlantic waves — completely free and spectacular in winter.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a local community swimming pool — Reykjanesbaer Swimming Pool (Grindavikurlaug or nearby) — a true budget Icelandic hot spring experience used by locals. Entry approx. 1,000–1,200 ISK. Soak in the geothermal hot pots and relax under the winter sky.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with honey and coffee at resort. Approx. 500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed wrap and fruit eaten at the lighthouse or lava field area. Approx. 800 ISK.
meals.dinner: Supermarket grocery run — buy fresh Icelandic lamb or fish and cook at resort. Approx. 1,500–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Municipal swimming pools are the most authentic and affordable hot spring experience in Iceland. Always shower without a swimsuit before entering as per Icelandic etiquette. Bring your own towel to avoid rental fees.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the South Coast. Drive to Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk behind the curtain of water (free entry, parking fee approx. 700 ISK). Continue to Skogafoss waterfall, equally dramatic and free to visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the black sand beach at Reynisfjara — one of the most stunning beaches in the world with basalt column formations and sea stacks. Free entry. Walk along the beach and admire the powerful Atlantic waves (stay behind safety markers — waves are dangerous).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward the resort. Stop in a dark rural area for Northern Lights viewing. January offers excellent aurora opportunities on clear nights. Return to resort by 22:00.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast at resort — bread, eggs, and coffee. Approx. 700 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch eaten at Skogafoss or Reynisfjara. Approx. 900 ISK.
meals.dinner: Stop at Vik village (N1 gas station restaurant) for a budget soup and bread meal. Approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: South Coast drive is approximately 2.5–3 hours each way from Reykjavik. Start early (by 09:00) to maximize the limited daylight hours. Check road.is for road conditions — Route 1 is generally well-maintained but can be icy.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning at the resort. Catch up on journaling, photos, or planning. Take a short walk along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjavik Botanical Garden (Grasagardur) — free entry, peaceful even in winter. Walk through the nearby Laugardalur valley park area. Visit Laugardalslaug — Reykjavik's largest public swimming pool and hot spring complex. Entry approx. 1,200 ISK.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Reykjavik flea market area or browse local charity shops on Laugavegur for budget souvenirs. Return to resort for a self-catered dinner and Northern Lights watch from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Skyr parfait with berries and granola at resort. Approx. 700 ISK.
meals.lunch: Bonus supermarket deli section — ready-made salads and sandwiches. Approx. 900–1,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Self-catered fish stew using fresh Icelandic cod or haddock from the supermarket. Approx. 1,500–2,000 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Laugardalslaug is a favorite among locals and a wonderful geothermal hot spring experience. The outdoor hot pots are perfect for stargazing and Northern Lights watching on clear evenings.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Perlan Museum in Reykjavik — the building itself sits atop six geothermal hot water tanks. The outdoor observation deck has a free viewing area with panoramic city views. The Northern Lights planetarium show inside is worth the ticket (approx. 2,800 ISK) for aurora education.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike up Esja Mountain (free) — a popular local hiking area with trails for all levels. The Steinn trail is manageable in winter with proper footwear. Views over Reykjavik and the bay are stunning.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights dedicated viewing night. Drive 20–30 minutes outside Reykjavik to a dark area (Thingvellir direction or coastal roads). Bring thermos of hot chocolate, blankets, and patience. Best viewing between 21:00–01:00.

meals.breakfast: Bread with Icelandic butter and smoked salmon from supermarket. Approx. 900 ISK.
meals.lunch: Perlan museum cafe for a light soup (approx. 1,800 ISK) or packed lunch brought from resort.
meals.dinner: Self-catered at resort — hearty lamb soup (kjötsúpa) made from supermarket ingredients. Approx. 1,200–1,800 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Esja Mountain trails can be icy and slippery in January. Rent or bring microspike crampons (available at outdoor rental shops for approx. 1,500 ISK/day). Never hike alone in winter conditions.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Snaefellsnes Peninsula day trip (long day — start by 07:30). Drive north to Kirkjufell mountain — one of Iceland's most photographed mountains, with a small waterfall beside it (free). Dramatic winter scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Snaefellsjokull National Park — the glacier volcano made famous by Jules Verne. Walk along the free coastal trails and lava fields. Visit Djupalonssandur black pebble beach with rusted shipwreck remains (free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back toward Reykjavik (approx. 2.5 hours). Stop for Northern Lights viewing on the way back through dark rural roads. Return to resort by 22:00–23:00.

meals.breakfast: Very early packed breakfast at resort before departure. Approx. 600 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed supermarket lunch eaten at Kirkjufell or Djupalonssandur. Approx. 900 ISK.
meals.dinner: Stop at a gas station (N1 or Olis) for budget hot soup or a sandwich on the return drive. Approx. 1,200–1,800 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Snaefellsnes is a long day trip (~5 hours total driving). Roads can be challenging in January — check road.is before departing. This is one of the most rewarding free day trips in Iceland.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning after the long Snaefellsnes day. Sleep in. Visit a local Reykjavik neighborhood cafe for a slow breakfast. Explore the 101 Reykjavik district on foot — street art, colorful buildings, and local culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the National Museum of Iceland (Thjodminjasafn) — entry approx. 2,500 ISK, offering deep insight into Icelandic history and Viking heritage. Walk to the nearby Reykjavik City Library (free) for warmth and rest.
day_by_day.evening: Hot spring evening at Nautholsvik Geothermal Beach — a unique outdoor geothermal lagoon on the Reykjavik seafront. Admission is free or very low cost (approx. 600 ISK). Soak in warm geothermal water while looking out at the ocean.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery (Sandholt or similar) — fresh pastry and coffee. Approx. 1,200–1,500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Supermarket grab-and-go. Approx. 800–1,000 ISK.
meals.dinner: Cook at resort — Icelandic lamb chops or skyr-marinated chicken with roasted vegetables. Approx. 2,000–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Nautholsvik is a hidden gem and very popular with locals. Check opening hours in advance as they vary seasonally. Bring a towel and swimsuit.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Reykjavik Art Museum (Listasafn Reykjavikur) — one ticket covers all three locations and costs approx. 1,800 ISK. Start with Hafnarhus (harbor house) for contemporary art exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the Grotta Lighthouse trail on Seltjarnarnes Peninsula (free) — a beautiful coastal walk with views of Reykjavik and excellent Northern Lights viewing location. The lighthouse sits on a small tidal island accessible at low tide.
day_by_day.evening: Dedicated Northern Lights photography and viewing session at Grotta or drive to Thingvellir for darker skies. This is one of the best Northern Lights viewing spots near Reykjavik. Stay out until midnight if aurora activity is high.

meals.breakfast: Oatmeal with banana and honey at resort. Approx. 500 ISK.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the Grotta Peninsula. Approx. 800 ISK.
meals.dinner: Tryggvaskali or a budget Reykjavik restaurant for traditional Icelandic lamb soup (kjötsúpa) — approx. 1,800–2,500 ISK.

day_by_day.notes: Grotta lighthouse area floods at high tide — check tide tables before walking to the island. The peninsula is one of the best free aurora viewing spots near the city with minimal light pollution.

day_by_day.morning: Final full day — revisit favorite spots or explore anything missed. Consider a visit to Videy Island (ferry approx. 1,500 ISK return) — a peaceful small island near Reykjavik with Yoko Ono's Imagine Peace Tower (lit in winter months).
day_by_day.afternoon: Last hot spring experience — visit Laugardalslaug or another municipal pool for a final relaxing geothermal soak. Pick up budget-friendly souvenirs at the Kolaportid flea market (open weekends) or Bonus supermarket (Icelandic chocolate, licorice, skyr snacks).
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights attempt — go to the best dark spot accessible from the resort. Celebrate the trip with a special dinner out. Pack bags and prepare for early departure logistics.

meals.breakfast: Celebratory resort breakfast — full spread of Icelandic skyr, bread, smoked fish, and coffee. Approx. 1,000 ISK.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a harbor cafe — fish soup and bread. Approx. 1,800–2,200 ISK.
meals.dinner: Treat yourself to a slightly nicer budget dinner — Saegreifinn (Sea Baron) restaurant for lobster soup and grilled fish skewers, approx. 2,500–3,500 ISK. An Icelandic institution.

day_by_day.notes: Saegreifinn is a beloved budget-friendly Reykjavik seafood spot — arrive early as it gets busy. This is the best value 'splurge' meal in the city. Confirm checkout time with the resort.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Store luggage if possible. Take a final walk along the beachfront to say goodbye to Iceland. Visit a local cafe for a farewell Icelandic coffee and kleinur (twisted doughnut).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, head to Keflavik Airport via Flybus shuttle (book in advance, approx. 3,000 ISK). Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for the shuttle ride and airport check-in. Browse duty-free for last-minute affordable Icelandic souvenirs (Icelandic wool products, lava salt, skyr).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with incredible memories of the Northern Lights, hot springs, dramatic landscapes, and Icelandic culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic pastry and coffee at a local bakery near the resort. Approx. 1,000–1,200 ISK.
meals.lunch: Light meal at Keflavik Airport or packed snacks from supermarket. Approx. 1,000–1,500 ISK.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport food depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Flybus return shuttle in advance at re.is to guarantee a seat. Arrive at Keflavik Airport at least 2 hours before international flights. Iceland's duty-free store at the airport often has good prices on Icelandic spirits and chocolate — compare prices before buying in the city.

trip_options.title: Classic Iceland Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange pre-booked airport transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, freshen up, and get a good night's rest to recover from travel fatigue.

meals.breakfast: On the flight
meals.lunch: On the flight or at airport
meals.dinner: Light snack from airport convenience store or 24-hour hotel service upon arrival

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — January nights in Iceland are long and cold (avg -1°C to 3°C). Pre-book airport transfer in advance. Check the aurora forecast app (Vedur.is) before sleeping — there may be a surprise northern lights display visible from the resort grounds on your first night!

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from travel. After a leisurely breakfast, take a slow orientation walk around the Aegean Bliss Resort beachfront area. Enjoy the dramatic Icelandic winter coastline, black sand, and crashing Atlantic waves. Sunrise is around 11:00 AM in January — time your walk to catch the golden hour light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head into Reykjavík (approx. 40–50 min drive or bus) for the Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour. Explore the colorful streets of the capital, visit Hallgrímskirkja church, and sample traditional Icelandic dishes including skyr, lamb soup, and fermented shark on this guided cultural experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort area. Check the northern lights forecast on Vedur.is. If cloud cover is low (rating 3+), head to a dark spot near the beachfront for your first potential aurora sighting. Bundle up in all your layers.

meals.breakfast: Buffet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — included or mid-range hotel dining
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings included on the Food & Culture Walking Tour
meals.dinner: Grillið or Café Loki in Reykjavík — try traditional Icelandic lamb stew and rye bread (budget ~4,000–6,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: January daylight is only about 5 hours in Iceland (11:00 AM–4:00 PM). Plan all outdoor sightseeing within this window. Download the Vedur.is aurora forecast app immediately — you'll use it every evening.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa (pre-booking essential — book weeks in advance). The lagoon is only 20 minutes from the resort. Arrive for a morning session to beat crowds. Soak in the iconic milky-blue 38–40°C mineral-rich waters, enjoy a silica mud mask, and relax in the steam caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue enjoying the Blue Lagoon — upgrade to include an in-water massage or lava restaurant lunch if budget allows. Depart by mid-afternoon. Stop at the nearby Reykjanes Peninsula lava fields for a short scenic walk and dramatic volcanic landscape photography.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — join an evening guided super jeep tour departing from the Reykjavík/Reykjanes area. Expert guides drive you away from light pollution into the dark Icelandic wilderness to maximize aurora viewing chances. Tour typically runs 8 PM–midnight.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort
meals.lunch: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon (mid-range option: soup and bread package ~3,500 ISK) or pack a light lunch
meals.dinner: Quick dinner before the super jeep tour — Bryggjan Brugghús gastropub in Grindavík area or a packed meal from a local bakery

day_by_day.notes: Blue Lagoon MUST be pre-booked online — walk-ins are rarely available. Comfort package (~12,000–15,000 ISK) is the best mid-range option. Remove jewelry before entering — silica can damage metals. Super jeep tour cost approx. 10,000–14,000 ISK per person.

day_by_day.morning: Rest morning if the super jeep tour ran late. After breakfast, drive or take a tour bus along the famous Golden Circle route. First stop: Þingvellir (Thingvellir) National Park — walk between the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates in the rift valley, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Golden Circle: Visit the mighty Geysir geothermal area and watch Strokkur erupt every 5–10 minutes shooting boiling water 20–30 meters into the air. Then head to the spectacular Gullfoss waterfall — Iceland's most iconic cascade, partially frozen in January for a magical winter scene.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the resort. If energy allows, set an aurora alarm for midnight and check the forecast. The Golden Circle area away from Reykjavík is excellent for dark-sky aurora viewing on the drive back.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Geysir Center café or Gullfoss Café — lamb soup and Icelandic bread (~2,500–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Lindin Restaurant in Laugarvatn village (on the Golden Circle route) — cozy Icelandic country dining, or cook a simple meal at the resort if kitchen available

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip from the resort. Roads in January can be icy — check road conditions at Road.is before departing. Rent a 4WD vehicle for safety. Dress in waterproof layers at Gullfoss — the mist from the waterfall creates an icy spray.

day_by_day.morning: Slow morning. Visit the Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) in Flúðir — Iceland's oldest natural swimming pool dating to 1891. A more authentic, less touristy alternative to the Blue Lagoon. Soak in the 38–40°C natural hot spring surrounded by geothermal steam vents and a small geyser. (~1.5 hour drive from resort)
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Flúðir village and its greenhouse tomato farms (Iceland grows vegetables geothermally). On the return journey, stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake — a stunning red and black caldera with vivid blue-green water, particularly dramatic in winter light.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a quiet dinner and prepare for tomorrow's adventure. Set aurora alerts — clear January nights in rural Iceland offer excellent aurora probability.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Minibar or packed lunch from a local supermarket (Krónan or Bónus) — save budget for dinner
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort restaurant or nearby local restaurant — try Icelandic fish stew (plokkfiskur) (~3,500–5,000 ISK)

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon entry is approx. 3,000 ISK per person — much more affordable than Blue Lagoon. Bring your own towel or rent one on-site. Kerið crater has a small entry fee (~700 ISK). Roads to Flúðir are generally paved but check conditions at Road.is.

day_by_day.morning: Drive south along the famous South Coast of Iceland. First stop: Seljalandsfoss waterfall — walk BEHIND the curtain of falling water (dress for getting very wet and icy). Then visit the hidden Gljúfrabúi canyon waterfall just 500m away.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue east to Skógafoss waterfall — one of Iceland's largest and most dramatic. Climb the 527 steps to the top viewing platform for sweeping views over the black sand coast. Then drive to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík — marvel at the basalt column sea stacks (Reynisdrangar) and powerful Atlantic surf. STAY BEHIND SAFETY BARRIERS — sneaker waves are deadly.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a guesthouse or stay in Vík area if doing a multi-day South Coast trip, OR return to Aegean Bliss Resort (approx. 2.5 hours). If returning, watch for auroras on the dark drive home.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Black Beach Restaurant in Vík — great views, Icelandic fish and chips (~3,000–4,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Suður-Vík Restaurant in Vík village for hearty lamb soup and fresh fish, or resort dinner on return

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day (~400 km round trip from resort). Start by 9:00 AM to maximize the 5 hours of daylight. Seljalandsfoss walkway behind the falls may be CLOSED in icy conditions — check ahead. Reynisfjara sneaker waves claim lives every year — never turn your back on the ocean.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge day. Sleep in, enjoy a long hotel breakfast, and spend the morning relaxing at the beachfront resort. Journal, read, or simply watch the dramatic winter waves. This mid-trip rest day is important for a 13-day journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Reykjanes Peninsula geothermal area near the resort — explore the Gunnuhver hot spring mud pools (one of Iceland's most powerful geothermal areas), the Bridge Between Continents (walk between tectonic plates), and the Reykjanesviti lighthouse on dramatic coastal cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — book a second aurora tour for another chance at the lights with expert guidance. Alternatively, self-drive to a dark area near the resort and wait with a thermos of hot chocolate.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Café at Reykjanes area or packed lunch
meals.dinner: Við Tjörnina restaurant in Reykjavík for upscale-casual Icelandic cuisine (mid-range splurge night: ~6,000–9,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Gunnuhver mud pools are free to visit but stay strictly on the boardwalks — the ground around geothermal areas is dangerously thin. The sulfur smell is intense! This is a great photography location. Consider this your 'splurge dinner' night.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip north to Snæfellsnes Peninsula (approx. 2.5 hours from resort). Visit the mystical Snæfellsjökull glacier volcano — immortalized in Jules Verne's 'Journey to the Center of the Earth.' Walk along the dramatic lava fields of Lóndrangar basalt pinnacles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the charming fishing village of Arnarstapi with its natural arch sea stacks and bird cliffs. Visit Kirkjufell mountain — Iceland's most photographed peak — and the adjacent Kirkjufellsfoss waterfall. In January, there's a chance of seeing the northern lights reflected in the falls at dusk.
day_by_day.evening: Begin the drive back south. Stop at a dark roadside pull-off to scan for auroras before returning to the resort. Snæfellsnes is far from light pollution — excellent aurora territory.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Fjöruhúsið café in Hellnar — famous for their soup and cake with ocean views (iconic Icelandic café experience, ~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Hotel restaurant on return, or pick up groceries from a Snæfellsnes village store for a simple self-prepared meal

day_by_day.notes: This is a very long driving day (~5–6 hours total driving). Consider staying overnight in Snæfellsnes if budget allows (guesthouses from ~15,000 ISK/night) to reduce driving stress and gain more exploration time. Road 54 around the peninsula is paved but can be icy in January.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Landmannalaugar Hot Spring area — note that the full highland F-road route is CLOSED in winter (January). Instead, join an organized winter super jeep tour to Landmannalaugar (departing from Reykjavík) — the only safe way to access this area in January. Trek through rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains and soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the Landmannalaugar guided experience — hike the surrounding obsidian lava fields (Laugahraun), admire the multi-colored mountains of red, green, yellow, and purple rhyolite, and enjoy the surreal steaming landscape. The hot spring soak at the end of a cold hike is unforgettable.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Reykjavík/resort with the tour group. Enjoy a well-earned hot shower and hearty dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early tour departure
meals.lunch: Pack a thermos of soup and sandwiches — there are no restaurants at Landmannalaugar in winter
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur restaurant in Reykjavík — modern Icelandic cuisine with traditional recipes (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: CRITICAL: Landmannalaugar is ONLY accessible in January via organized super jeep tours with experienced highland guides. DO NOT attempt to drive there independently — the F-roads are completely impassable and dangerous. Tour cost approx. 18,000–25,000 ISK per person. Book well in advance as winter tours fill up quickly. Bring a swimsuit for the hot spring pool.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Reykjavík more deeply. Visit the National Museum of Iceland to understand 1,100 years of Icelandic history and Viking heritage. Walk through the old harbor area (Grandi) with its colorful fishing boats and new food hall.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Perlan museum — a stunning glass dome building with a real indoor ice cave, Northern Lights planetarium show, and panoramic views over Reykjavík and the surrounding mountains and ocean. The Northern Lights show inside is excellent for understanding the science of auroras.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Reykjavík's famous nightlife and bar scene on Laugavegur street — Iceland's main shopping and entertainment strip. Visit a craft beer bar like Skúli Craft Bar or Kaldi Bar. Return to resort by late evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Grandi Mathöll food hall in the harbor — try fish tacos, Icelandic hot dogs (pylsur), and local craft beer (~2,000–3,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: Sægreifinn (Sea Baron) restaurant in the old harbor — famous for lobster soup and grilled fish on a stick (~3,000–4,500 ISK) — a true Reykjavík institution

day_by_day.notes: Perlan museum entry is approx. 4,990 ISK — worth every króna for the ice cave and aurora show. The Reykjavík City Card (available for 24/48/72 hours) covers many museum entries and public transport — check if it's cost-effective for your remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Take a whale watching tour from Reykjavík Old Harbor (winter tours available — humpback whales are often spotted year-round). Dress in extreme warmth — the boat deck is brutally cold in January. Tour runs approximately 3 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Settlement Exhibition (Landnámssýningin) — an underground museum built around actual Viking-age ruins discovered beneath Reykjavík. Then walk to the Harpa Concert Hall, a stunning geometric glass building on the harbor — free to enter and explore the interior architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Final Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep — book this as your 'last chance' aurora tour if you haven't seen them clearly yet. Many operators offer a 'come again free' guarantee if lights don't appear. Alternatively, self-drive to the Reykjanes Peninsula dark areas near the resort.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before whale watching departure
meals.lunch: Reykjavík harbor area — try a classic Icelandic hot dog from Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur (the famous hot dog stand, ~600 ISK) and soup from a nearby café
meals.dinner: Fiskfélagið (Fish Company) restaurant — excellent Icelandic seafood in a mid-range setting (~5,000–7,000 ISK per person)

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January has a good success rate for humpback whales but seas can be rough — take seasickness medication if needed. Dress in every layer you own — the wind chill on deck is extreme. Elding and Special Tours are reputable operators (~10,000–12,000 ISK per person).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the geothermal swimming pools of Reykjavík — try Laugardalslaug (the largest outdoor pool complex) or the iconic Sundhöllin pool in the city center. Icelanders swim outdoors year-round — it's a wonderful cultural experience to soak in a hot pot at -2°C with snow falling around you.
day_by_day.afternoon: Souvenir shopping on Laugavegur street — browse Icelandic wool sweaters (lopapeysa), lava jewelry, Viking crafts, and local food products like skyr, licorice, and Brennivín (Icelandic schnapps). Visit the Kolaportið flea market if it's the weekend for local finds.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a special Reykjavík restaurant. Splurge slightly for your last full evening — try Dill Restaurant (Nordic fine dining, Iceland's first Michelin-starred restaurant) for a special experience, or Grillmarkaðurinn for excellent Icelandic grilled meats and seafood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a bakery — Brauð & Co. for exceptional Icelandic sourdough and pastries (~1,500–2,000 ISK)
meals.dinner: Farewell splurge dinner: Grillmarkaðurinn (~7,000–10,000 ISK per person) or Dill Restaurant tasting menu (~15,000+ ISK) — choose based on budget comfort

day_by_day.notes: Icelandic swimming pool etiquette is important — you MUST shower thoroughly without a swimsuit before entering the pool. Attendants enforce this. Entry to public pools is approx. 1,050 ISK. For souvenirs, 66°North outlet store offers quality Icelandic outdoor clothing at reduced prices.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — pack and check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. If time allows before airport transfer, take one last walk along the beachfront to soak in the dramatic Icelandic coastline, listen to the waves, and say goodbye to this extraordinary landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Keflavík International Airport (20–40 minutes from resort depending on exact location). Arrive at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for international flights. Browse duty-free for last-minute Icelandic spirits, chocolate, or skincare products (Blue Lagoon products available in airport).
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland — carry memories of geothermal pools, aurora-lit skies, volcanic landscapes, and the warmth of Icelandic hospitality.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly
meals.lunch: Airport restaurant or café — Fljótt og Gott at Keflavík airport for Icelandic lamb soup one last time (~2,500 ISK)
meals.dinner: On the flight home

day_by_day.notes: Keflavík Airport is 50 km from Reykjavík and 20–40 min from the Reykjanes/resort area. The Flybus connects Reykjavík BSÍ terminal to the airport (~3,000 ISK). Leave extra time in January for potential icy road delays. Blue Lagoon duty-free skincare makes excellent gifts. Skyr and Icelandic chocolate are allowed in carry-on luggage.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Iceland Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep
experiences.description: Join a guided super jeep tour into the Icelandic wilderness away from city light pollution for the best chance of witnessing the aurora borealis. Expert guides track solar activity and cloud cover in real time to maximize your viewing experience. Hot chocolate and warm blankets provided.

experiences.name: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa
experiences.description: Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Enjoy in-water massages, silica mud masks, and a swim-up bar. Booking in advance is essential. The surreal lava field backdrop makes this one of Iceland's most iconic hot spring experiences.

experiences.name: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak
experiences.description: Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, this rustic geothermal pool sits amid bubbling hot springs and a small geyser. A truly authentic and affordable Icelandic bathing tradition.

experiences.name: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour
experiences.description: Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes like skyr, lamb soup, fresh langoustine, and Icelandic hot dogs at Bæjarins Beztu. Visit the iconic Hallgrímskirkja church and the Settlement Exhibition museum to dive into Norse culture.

experiences.name: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike
experiences.description: Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains in the Fjallabak Nature Reserve and reward yourself with a natural geothermal hot spring soak at the end. The contrast of steaming hot springs against snow-dusted neon-hued peaks is utterly surreal and unforgettable.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – Flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Keflavík International Airport at 22:30. Private luxury transfer arranged to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check-in, unwind with a welcome drink and late-night room service. If skies are clear, step outside for a spontaneous first glimpse of the Northern Lights from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: On-board or at airport lounge
meals.lunch: On-board or at airport lounge
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort – request the chef's premium cold-cut and seafood platter with Icelandic skyr dessert

day_by_day.notes: Keep luggage minimal for the transfer. Confirm concierge wake-up preferences and Northern Lights alert service upon check-in. January darkness means aurora activity can begin as early as 17:00 local time.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely late start to recover from travel. Enjoy the resort's gourmet breakfast with panoramic ocean views. Explore the beachfront and resort amenities, including any private hot tub or geothermal pool on-site.
day_by_day.afternoon: Blue Lagoon Geothermal Spa – Soak in the world-famous milky-blue geothermal waters rich in silica and minerals. Book the premium 'Retreat Spa' package including in-water massage, silica mud mask, algae mask, and access to the exclusive Retreat Lounge. The Blue Lagoon is only 20 minutes from the resort.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at the Blue Lagoon's signature LAVA Restaurant overlooking the steaming lava fields and geothermal waters. Return to resort for an early night and Northern Lights alert monitoring.

meals.breakfast: Full Icelandic gourmet breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort – skyr parfait, smoked salmon, rye bread, and eggs
meals.lunch: Light snack at Blue Lagoon's in-water bar – Langoustine soup and sparkling water
meals.dinner: LAVA Restaurant at Blue Lagoon – Arctic char, Icelandic lamb, and local craft beer or wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Book Blue Lagoon Retreat Spa well in advance – slots fill up fast. Bring a hair conditioner or use theirs to protect hair from silica. January temperatures around -2°C to 4°C, so the warm lagoon is especially magical.

day_by_day.morning: Reykjavik Food & Culture Walking Tour – Depart by private car to Reykjavik (45 min). Explore Iceland's vibrant capital through its food scene and Viking heritage. Sample traditional dishes including hákarl (fermented shark), skyr, lamb soup, and Icelandic hot dogs at the famous Bæjarins Beztu Pylsur stand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Reykjavik: visit Hallgrímskirkja Church (stunning views from the tower), the Sun Voyager sculpture, and the Harpa Concert Hall. Browse luxury Icelandic design boutiques for wool sweaters (lopapeysa) and local artisan goods.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep – Join a guided super jeep tour departing from Reykjavik into the Icelandic wilderness, away from city light pollution. Expert guides use aurora forecasts to find the best viewing spots. Hot chocolate and blankets provided on tour.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Tasting stops on the Food & Culture Walking Tour – multiple venues included
meals.dinner: Dill Restaurant, Reykjavik – Iceland's only Michelin-starred restaurant. Nordic tasting menu with local, seasonal ingredients and wine pairing. Reserve weeks in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Wear warm, layered clothing for the evening Super Jeep tour. Northern Lights sightings depend on cloud cover and solar activity – guides will reschedule if conditions are poor. January KP index is often favorable.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided Golden Circle tour – Visit Þingvellir National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site, where the American and Eurasian tectonic plates meet), the erupting Strokkur Geyser at the Geysir geothermal area, and Gullfoss Waterfall. Private luxury SUV with expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue Golden Circle with a stop at Kerið volcanic crater lake. If time permits, visit the Friðheimar greenhouse farm for a tomato soup lunch experience inside a geothermal greenhouse.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Enjoy a private in-suite spa treatment (arrange with concierge in advance) or relax in the resort's geothermal facilities. Monitor Northern Lights alerts for a potential late-night viewing from the resort grounds.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Friðheimar Greenhouse Restaurant – tomato soup, fresh bread, and Bloody Mary made with homegrown tomatoes
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – Icelandic lamb rack with root vegetable purée and local craft spirits

day_by_day.notes: Golden Circle is approximately 300 km round trip. Roads in January can be icy – private driver is essential. Pack hand warmers and waterproof boots for outdoor stops.

day_by_day.morning: Secret Lagoon (Gamla Laugin) Soak – Drive to Flúðir village (approx. 1.5 hrs). Experience Iceland's oldest swimming pool, a natural hot spring dating back to 1891. Far less crowded than the Blue Lagoon, with an authentic and intimate atmosphere surrounded by geothermal activity and small geysers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the rural Icelandic countryside around Flúðir. Visit local farm stalls for homemade Icelandic preserves, wool products, and dairy. Stop at Skálholt Cathedral, one of Iceland's most historically significant religious sites.
day_by_day.evening: Return to resort. Sunset (around 16:30 in January) drive along the coastal route for dramatic winter photography. Evening at leisure – consider booking the resort's private chef dinner experience in your suite.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Traditional Icelandic lamb stew at a local restaurant in Flúðir village
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner in-suite at Aegean Bliss Resort – curated 4-course Icelandic tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Secret Lagoon water temperature is around 38–40°C year-round. Bring a swimsuit and towel, though rentals are available. The lagoon is surrounded by small geysers that erupt periodically – a unique experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of the Reykjanes Peninsula and surrounding volcanic landscapes. Fly over lava fields, geothermal vents, and coastal cliffs. Land on a remote glacier or lava plateau for a champagne toast (arrange with local heli-tour operators through concierge).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Bridge Between Continents walkway on the Reykjanes Peninsula – walk between the Eurasian and North American tectonic plates. Explore the Reykjanesviti Lighthouse (Iceland's oldest) and the dramatic Gunnuhver mud pools.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (second attempt if first was clouded out, or a different route for new scenery). Expert guides take you to remote highland locations with zero light pollution for maximum aurora visibility.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic basket prepared by resort chef – enjoyed at a scenic coastal viewpoint on the Reykjanes Peninsula
meals.dinner: Grillið Restaurant at Radisson Blu Saga Hotel, Reykjavik – panoramic city views, premium Icelandic seafood and lamb

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours must be booked well in advance and are weather-dependent. January offers dramatic low-light photography conditions. Super Jeep evening tour – dress in thermal layers, waterproof outer shell, and insulated boots.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the resort. Sleep in, enjoy a spa treatment (hot stone massage or geothermal facial), and take a winter beach walk along the beachfront. Capture dramatic January seascape photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private snowmobile or ATV tour on a nearby lava field or coastal terrain (arrange through concierge with local operators). Alternatively, visit the nearby Viking World Museum in Reykjanesbær for an immersive insight into Iceland's Norse heritage.
day_by_day.afternoon_alt: Visit the Icelandic Museum of Rock 'n' Roll in Keflavík for a quirky cultural afternoon experience.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private Northern Lights photography workshop – hire a professional aurora photographer to guide you to prime locations and teach long-exposure night photography techniques. Return to resort for a late dinner.

meals.breakfast: Extended resort brunch – eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Resort poolside or lounge lunch – lobster bisque and open-faced shrimp sandwich
meals.dinner: Late dinner at resort restaurant – pan-seared cod with dill butter, roasted potatoes, and a glass of premium white Burgundy

day_by_day.notes: Mid-trip rest day is important given the active schedule. January daylight is only 5–6 hours, so maximize outdoor time between 11:00 and 15:30. Northern Lights photography workshop requires a DSLR or mirrorless camera with manual settings.

day_by_day.morning: South Coast adventure – Private guided day tour eastward along Iceland's dramatic South Coast. First stop: Seljalandsfoss Waterfall (you can walk behind the cascading water). Then Skógafoss Waterfall, one of Iceland's largest and most iconic falls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the black sand beach of Reynisfjara near Vík, famous for its basalt column formations and dramatic sea stacks (Reynisdrangar). Visit the charming village of Vík í Mýrdal and the striking hilltop Vík Church.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive along the South Coast with potential Northern Lights viewing en route. Arrive back at resort by 20:00–21:00. Relaxing evening with room service or late resort dining.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before early departure
meals.lunch: Skál! Restaurant in Vík – Icelandic fish and chips, lamb burger, and local beer
meals.dinner: Resort restaurant or in-suite dining – slow-cooked Icelandic lamb shank with root vegetables and red wine reduction

day_by_day.notes: Reynisfjara beach has extremely dangerous sneaker waves – stay behind the safety markers and never turn your back to the ocean. Walking behind Seljalandsfoss is possible in January but paths may be icy – use microspikes (available from guide).

day_by_day.morning: Landmannalaugar Hot Spring Hike – Depart by super jeep into the Fjallabak Nature Reserve. Trek through Iceland's stunning rainbow-colored rhyolite mountains. The landscape is otherworldly with obsidian lava fields, steaming fumaroles, and snow-dusted peaks. Soak in the natural geothermal hot spring pool at the end of the hike.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Landmannalaugar area. Visit the dramatic Ljótipollur explosion crater lake (vivid red volcanic earth contrasting with deep blue water). Enjoy hot soup and coffee from the super jeep's provisions amid the volcanic wilderness.
day_by_day.evening: Return journey to resort (approx. 3 hrs). Arrive by 19:00–20:00. Treat yourself to a restorative evening in the resort's geothermal pool or hot tub under the winter sky – prime Northern Lights viewing position.

meals.breakfast: Hearty resort breakfast before the demanding hike
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch provided by resort chef – thermos of lamb soup, rye bread sandwiches, Icelandic chocolate, and hot tea
meals.dinner: Resort fine dining – grilled Arctic char with fennel salad, capers, and citrus beurre blanc

day_by_day.notes: Landmannalaugar is only accessible by 4WD super jeep in winter. The hike is moderate difficulty – wear waterproof hiking boots and thermal layers. Bring a swimsuit for the geothermal pool. This is one of Iceland's most unique and rewarding experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Private ice cave tour in Þórsmörk or Mýrdalsjökull glacier area. A certified glacier guide leads you into a stunning natural ice cave with vivid blue and turquoise ice formations. Don crampons and a helmet for a safe, exhilarating experience inside a living glacier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Þórsmörk valley – a hidden paradise between three glaciers. Walk among birch forests and dramatic mountain ridges. The area is accessible only by super jeep river crossings, making it feel truly remote and exclusive.
day_by_day.evening: Northern Lights Hunt by Super Jeep (third opportunity – guides will target the best forecast location for the evening). Celebrate any sightings with a champagne toast in the wilderness.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Hot meal at Húsadalur mountain hut in Þórsmörk – lamb soup and fresh bread by a roaring fire
meals.dinner: Aegean Bliss Resort – 5-course tasting menu with Icelandic wine and spirits pairing, celebrating the halfway point of the trip

day_by_day.notes: Ice cave tours are only available in winter (November–March) when the ice is stable. Caves change each year – your guide will take you to the most spectacular currently accessible formation. Crampons and helmets are provided.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided whale watching tour from Reykjavik Old Harbour (January is humpback whale season). Board a luxury yacht or high-speed RIB boat for a 3-hour ocean excursion. Spot humpback whales, minke whales, and white-beaked dolphins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Reykjavik for an afternoon of culture. Visit the National Museum of Iceland for a deep dive into Icelandic history from settlement to modern day. Explore the Reykjavik Art Museum (Hafnarhús) for contemporary Icelandic art.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at a Reykjavik chef's table experience – book a private room at Óx or Matur og Drykkur for an intimate tasting menu celebrating Icelandic culinary heritage with modern Nordic techniques.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast
meals.lunch: Kopar Restaurant at Reykjavik Old Harbour – freshly caught fish of the day, lobster, and local craft beer
meals.dinner: Matur og Drykkur, Reykjavik – innovative Icelandic tasting menu based on a 1930s Icelandic cookbook, with natural wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Whale watching in January has excellent chances of humpback sightings. Dress in full waterproofs provided by the operator – it is cold and potentially rough at sea. Book chef's table dinner well in advance as seats are extremely limited.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely final full morning at the resort. Enjoy a long spa session – sauna, steam room, and geothermal pool. Reflect on the trip over a slow, indulgent breakfast. Optional: sunrise (around 10:45 in January) photography walk along the beachfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private falconry experience or horse riding on Icelandic horses (Icelandic horses are a unique, ancient breed known for their smooth tölt gait). Explore the coastal landscape on horseback with a private guide. Alternatively, visit the Keflavík area's geothermal bakery where bread is baked underground using geothermal heat.
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner at the resort's finest dining venue. Request a private table with ocean view. Toast the journey with Icelandic aquavit and a premium Champagne. Final Northern Lights vigil from the resort terrace or beach – this is the last opportunity for aurora viewing.

meals.breakfast: Champagne brunch at resort – eggs royale, smoked salmon, caviar blinis, fresh fruit, and Prosecco
meals.lunch: Light lunch at resort lounge – lobster sandwich and Icelandic herb salad
meals.dinner: Farewell 6-course gala dinner at Aegean Bliss Resort's signature restaurant – Icelandic langoustine, wild reindeer, skyr panna cotta, and a curated Scandinavian wine journey

day_by_day.notes: Pack bags this evening for an efficient morning departure. Tip guides, drivers, and resort staff appropriately – Icelanders appreciate but do not expect tips, though they are warmly received for exceptional service. Confirm departure transfer with concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning – enjoy a last Icelandic breakfast at the resort. Take a brief final walk along the beachfront to absorb the atmosphere one last time. Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort and board private luxury transfer to Keflavík International Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Airport departure. Use the premium lounge at Keflavík Airport. Consider a final stop at the Blue Lagoon Spa (located between the resort and airport) if your flight allows – many travelers book a final soak before departure. Blue Lagoon offers luggage storage and shower facilities.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Iceland with extraordinary memories of the Northern Lights, geothermal wonders, dramatic volcanic landscapes, and world-class Nordic cuisine.

meals.breakfast: Final Icelandic breakfast at resort – skyr with berries, smoked lamb, rye bread, and strong Icelandic coffee
meals.lunch: Airport lounge or Blue Lagoon café – light bites before departure
meals.dinner: On-board or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for airport security and check-in. If stopping at Blue Lagoon, book the Comfort package which includes entry, towel, and one drink. The Blue Lagoon is only 10 minutes from the airport. Take any remaining Icelandic currency – it is not widely accepted outside Iceland.
